# Code of Conduct

DTFS is a small project. This page says how we treat each other in issues, pull requests, discussions and every other project space.

## Expected

- Be respectful and assume good intent. Disagree about the code, not the person.
- Keep feedback specific and actionable: what is wrong, where, and what would fix it.
- Accept that a maintainer may decline a change. Ask why if the reason is unclear.
- Respect people's time: search existing issues first and give the details a bug report needs.

## Not accepted

- Harassment, insults, threats, or discriminatory jokes and language, about anyone, for any reason.
- Personal attacks, trolling, or sustained disruption of a discussion.
- Publishing someone else's private information (addresses, real names behind a handle, private messages) without their permission.
- Sexualised language or imagery.
- Anything else a reasonable person would consider inappropriate in a professional setting.

## Scope

This applies in every project space (repository, issues, pull requests, discussions, wiki) and when someone represents the project elsewhere.

## Reporting

Report a problem privately to the maintainer, [@lischetzke](https://github.com/lischetzke), through the contact options on that GitHub profile. Do not open a public issue for it. Reports are handled confidentially.

Security vulnerabilities are not conduct issues: report them through a [private security advisory](https://github.com/lischetzke/dtfs/security/advisories/new).

## Enforcement

The maintainer decides on reports and may, depending on severity, ask for a change in behaviour, edit or delete comments, lock threads, or block someone from the project temporarily or permanently. The maintainer is held to the same rules.

This text is inspired by the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/).
